newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Accord reached to end Colombia port strike.
newsitem.headline: Accord reached to end Colombia port strike.

text.p: Dock workers' representatives, ship owners and cargo operators reached agreement to end the nine-day- old strike in Colombia's Pacific coast port of Buenaventura, a union leader said Thursday.

The deal provides an increase in the rates paid to dock workers for handling a variety of different cargoes, social security, sickness and injury benefits and meal allowances. The dock workers will be informed of the accord this afternoon and the strike is expected to be lifted shortly after, the union official said.

"We have reached an agreement to end the strike we are now in the signing ceremony," Nelson Amaya, regional boss of the Unitary Workers' Confederation (CUT), told Reuters just before 1300 local/1800 GMT.

The main dock workers' union SINTRAMARITIMOS is affiliated to the CUT. A fourth point to the agreement opens the way for the creation of special committees to analyze the more complex issues related to port activities and the way dockers are contracted. Their work will begin once port operations return to normal, Amaya said.

The breakthrough comes after three days of talks in the provincial capital Cali. The terms of the accord will be explained to the 3,000 dock workers in Buenaventura this afternoon but the negotiating committee had full decision-making powers, thereby eliminating the need for workers to vote on the agreement at a general assembly.
A port spokesman said the port was losing $1 million for very day the strike lasted. It was not immediately known how long it would take to clear the cargo backlog.
